descriptionChirho: The gentilic noun 'Arabi designates a person (or people) from Arabia, used both in singular and plural forms. All four clusters refer to the same ethnic/geographic identity with only grammatical variation: singular vs. plural, with or without conjunctive waw, and different prepositions. Multilingual glosses confirm unity: Spanish 'arabe/arabes', Hindi 'Arabi/Arabiyon', Arabic 'al-Arabi/al-Arab', Korean 'Arabiain/Arab saramdeul', and Swahili 'Mwarabu/Waarabu' (singular/plural). No semantic distinction warrants separate senses.
